title: No one receives Jesus' testimony as he speaks it
english: [Origen resumes:] And his testimony no one receives. Yet many have received his testimony, as John himself again adds when he says, "The one who received his testimony has sealed that God is true" (John 3:33). How then can it be true, when some do receive his testimony, that "his testimony no one receives" (John 3:32)?

The difficulty raised must be resolved this way. Jesus, who has come from above and speaks what he heard and saw, offers the highest and very great testimony about the Father and himself. No one receives this testimony as he himself speaks it, because the hearers, though they have made a beginning of receiving, fall far short of the greatness of the testimony. Nevertheless, even if no one is able to receive his testimony in that way, still it is possible to receive it insofar as those who are just now approaching the faith are able to receive it.

title: Receiving Jesus' testimony and the unity of believers
english: So there is no contradiction between "the one who receives his testimony" and the statement that no one has received it, because it is received in one way and not in another. Those who have received Jesus' testimony set their seal with firm assent that God is true, having learned [the text breaks off here].

The word "one" is used in many ways, both according to likeness and according to many other things. It is used according to agreement, as when Scripture says, "The multitude of those who believed had one heart and one soul" (Acts 4:32). It is used according to likeness, as when it says, "For we were all baptized in one Spirit into one body" (1 Corinthians 12:13), according to likeness of nature. And just as we all, having Adam as our beginning and head according to the nature of our birth, are said to have one body, so also we inscribe Christ as our head through the divine regeneration, which has become for us a type of his death and resurrection. He rose as firstborn from the dead. We inscribe him as head according to the prefiguration of his resurrection, "of whom we are members in part and a body through the Spirit," being regenerated into incorruption [the text is corrupt here].
